entities.label: The Cover-Up
entities.sub: Operational domain - concealment run as a funded programme, not a passive silence
entities.desc: This board treats concealment as a discipline with doctrine, staffing and a budget line, because that is how the surviving record describes it. The 17 January 1953 Robertson Panel, convened by CIA's Office of Scientific Intelligence, did not merely conclude that sightings were harmless - it recommended that the national security agencies 'take immediate steps to strip the Unidentified Flying Objects of the special status they have been given and the aura of mystery they have unfortunately acquired', through a programme of mass-media debunking and the monitoring of civilian UFO groups. That is a covert influence recommendation written by an intelligence agency about its own public. Forty-four years later CIA historian Gerald K. Haines, writing in the agency's own classified-then-declassified journal Studies in Intelligence, admitted that Air Force officers had knowingly issued false explanations - natural phenomena, ice crystals, temperature inversions - to Congress and the public for sightings the Air Force knew were U-2 and OXCART overflights, and called this 'not the full story'. The documented route from ordinary secrecy into active concealment therefore runs through three mechanisms this board tracks separately: false official explanation, record destruction, and the redefinition of a programme so that the honest answer to a congressional question becomes technically 'no such programme exists'. GAO's 1995 search for Roswell records found that outgoing messages from Roswell Army Air Field for 1946-1949 had been destroyed with no disposition authority and no destruction certificate on file - a documented gap where the destruction itself is the evidence. To be scored highly on this domain is to be a producer of concealment rather than merely a person kept in the dark by it: an author of cover stories, a signatory on a destruction order, a briefer who gave a denial he knew to be false.

entities.label: Official Denial
entities.sub: Evidentiary domain - the denial as a dated, attributable artifact
entities.desc: A denial is not the end of an inquiry on this board; it is an entry in it. The editorial rule is that every official denial gets recorded in full, with its author, its date, its precise wording and its scope - because the wording and the scope are the data. AARO's Volume I historical record report of February 2024 states flatly that the office found 'no empirical evidence' that the US government or private companies have reverse-engineered extraterrestrial technology; what the same report also states is the scope of its search, the access it was granted, and which named programmes it did and did not resolve, and those are the parts a hostile audit turns on. The documented pattern that makes this a domain rather than a footnote is the historical one: the National Reconnaissance Office's very existence was an official secret from 1961 until 1992, meaning that for thirty-one years an accurate answer to 'does that organisation exist' was legally required to be no. Denials therefore have a known failure mode - a categorical denial by an official without the relevant read-in is not a statement about the world but a statement about that official's access. Scoring on this domain measures how central official denial has been to an entity's public conduct: an agency spokesman who issues denials, a director who signs them, or a witness whose testimony a denial was written to rebut.

entities.label: Secrecy Law & Classification
entities.sub: Legal domain - the statutory and executive machinery that makes concealment lawful
entities.desc: Everything this board describes is, on its face, legal - and that is the point. Classification authority flows from executive order rather than statute for most national security information, which means the same executive branch that runs a programme also decides whether Congress and the courts may learn of it. Layered on top are the Atomic Energy Act's 'born classified' Restricted Data regime, the Invention Secrecy Act's power to impose secrecy orders on patent applications, and 50 U.S.C. 3510's authority for unvouchered and confidential expenditure certified by agency heads rather than audited. The dual-use route into a concealment programme is simple and requires no conspiracy: an activity placed inside a special access programme, then waived from ordinary congressional notification under the exception in 10 U.S.C. 119, is protected by exactly the same machinery whether it holds a stealth aircraft or a recovered craft, and the machinery cannot tell the difference. Scoring high on this domain means an entity is a wielder of classification authority - an original classification authority, a security officer, a programme security manager - rather than a person subject to it.

entities.label: Secrecy Architecture
entities.sub: Structural domain - how compartments are stacked so that no single person sees the whole
entities.desc: Compartmentation is not a synonym for secrecy; it is a specific engineering choice about who may hold which fragment, and it is the single most important structural fact on this board. The Manhattan Project is the documented ancestor: tens of thousands of workers at Oak Ridge and Hanford who could describe their own task precisely and had no authorised knowledge of the weapon, with compartmentation enforced by physical separation, need-to-know and a security apparatus reporting outside the technical chain. Applied to a recovery and reverse-engineering effort, the same architecture produces the effect witnesses repeatedly describe: a metallurgist who can characterise a sample without being told where it came from, a security officer who moves the container without being told what is in it, a programme manager who signs the contract without the read-in that would let him understand it. The consequence for evidence is severe and must be stated plainly - a compartmented programme generates almost no witness who can testify to the whole, only many witnesses who can each testify to a fragment, which is precisely the evidentiary signature critics cite as weakness. Scoring high here means an entity sits at a junction where fragments were assembled: a control officer, a security review authority, or a person read into more than one compartment at once.

David Grusch testified before the House Oversight Committee on 26 July 2023 that he was denied access to programmes he had been directed to investigate, and that access denial itself was used as a concealment mechanism.

Compartmentation predicts the exact evidentiary pattern the disclosure fight exhibits - many partial witnesses, no complete one - which means the absence of a single comprehensive whistleblower is a consequence of the architecture rather than evidence against the programme. Reasoning: this is the documented Manhattan Project effect applied to a smaller population.

entities.label: Special Access Programs
entities.sub: Access-control domain - the SAP/USAP/waived tier and its oversight carve-outs
entities.desc: A special access programme is the mechanism by which the executive branch creates an information space with tighter controls than Top Secret and a smaller list of people who may enter it. The tier structure is documented policy, not speculation: acknowledged SAPs whose existence is public though their content is not; unacknowledged SAPs whose very existence is classified; and waived unacknowledged SAPs for which the Secretary of Defense has exercised the 10 U.S.C. 119 waiver so that notification runs only to the chairs and ranking members of the armed services and defence appropriations committees - eight members, typically without staff, typically orally. That last category is the load-bearing one for this board, because it is a lawful configuration in which a programme can run for decades while the overwhelming majority of Congress has no lawful means of learning it exists. In 2009 the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence prepared an information memorandum reviewing a request to convert DIA's advanced aerospace work into a special access programme - a documented instance of the transition being considered for exactly this subject matter. Scoring high on this domain means an entity held, granted, or was formally denied SAP-level access, and the denial is scored as heavily as the grant.

entities.label: Psychological Operations & Perception Management
entities.sub: Operational domain - deliberate manipulation of belief as a security measure
entities.desc: The use of the UFO subject as a vehicle for deception against a domestic audience is documented at the level of an official recommendation and at the level of a named case. The recommendation is the Robertson Panel's January 1953 proposal for a debunking campaign using mass media, psychiatrists and advertising specialists, explicitly aimed at reducing public susceptibility rather than at establishing what the objects were. The named case is Paul Bennewitz, an Albuquerque physicist living beside Kirtland AFB, who in the early 1980s was fed fabricated documents and staged material by Air Force Office of Special Investigations personnel - most prominently Richard C. Doty, whose later New Mexico State Police personnel file was released under public records law and runs to 321 pages - with the documented effect of destroying his mental health. The dual-use route is exact: a genuine sensitive programme adjacent to a witness generates a security problem, and the cheapest solution is not to silence the witness but to discredit him by feeding him something absurd and letting him repeat it. That mechanism cuts in both directions and must be applied honestly - it explains real disinformation injected into the field, and it is also the most common frame used to dismiss testimony that is not disinformation. Scoring high here means an entity ran, authored or knowingly transmitted deception material.

entities.label: Disinformation & Fabricated Documents
entities.sub: Evidentiary domain - forged and salted records as a concealment instrument
entities.desc: A body of fabricated documents is the most efficient way to poison an evidentiary well, and this field has one of the largest such bodies on record. The Majestic-12 papers - first surfacing on unsolicited film delivered to Jaime Shandera in December 1984, purporting to be an Eisenhower-era briefing on recovered craft - were investigated by the FBI, whose file on the matter is public in the Bureau's Vault reading room and records the Air Force Office of Special Investigations' assessment that the documents were bogus. Whether any given MJ-12 document is a forgery, a forgery built on real classified content, or a genuine record does not change the structural point: once fabricated material enters circulation, every genuine document acquires the burden of proving it is not one of them, and that burden is the concealment dividend. This board therefore treats forged documents as evidence of an act - someone made them, at a cost, for a purpose - and asks who benefited from their circulation. Scoring high on this domain means an entity authored, distributed, authenticated or debunked fabricated material, all four of which are consequential roles.

entities.label: Counterintelligence
entities.sub: Operational domain - the security service pointed inward at the programme's own people
entities.desc: Counterintelligence is the function that protects a programme from penetration, and in a compartmented programme it is also the function that protects the programme from its own personnel. The tools are ordinary and documented: polygraph, continuous evaluation, security clearance adjudication, non-disclosure agreements with criminal penalties, and the authority to revoke access administratively without the due process that attaches to a criminal charge. That last power is the one that matters most here, because clearance revocation is effectively unreviewable and can end a career without any finding of wrongdoing ever being made or defended. AFOSI is the service that recurs across this board's cases - Kirtland in 1980, Bennewitz in the early 1980s - and its charter combines criminal investigation with counterintelligence, which means the same organisation that protects a programme can open a criminal file on the person who talks about it. The dual-use route into concealment is therefore built into the job description rather than smuggled in. Scoring high on this domain means an entity exercised counterintelligence authority over others, or was the target of it in a way that is documented.

entities.label: Congressional Oversight
entities.sub: Institutional domain - the committees, clearances and gaps through which Congress does or does not see
entities.desc: Congressional oversight of the deepest access tiers is not a matter of will but of architecture, and the architecture is written down. Under 10 U.S.C. 119 the Secretary of Defense may waive notification of a special access programme so that only the chairs and ranking members of four defence committees are told - eight members, ordinarily without cleared staff, ordinarily orally, with no ability to take notes away or consult a colleague. A member outside that eight who suspects a programme exists has no lawful route to confirm it, and a member inside it has no lawful route to tell anyone. That is the structural fact the disclosure fight has been trying to break since 2017. The instruments Congress has reached for are traceable: mandatory reporting requirements in successive NDAAs, the creation of AARO with a statutory mandate to review the historical record, the Department of Defense Inspector General's evaluation DODIG-2023-109, and - on 9 September 2025 - a House Oversight hearing titled 'Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection' that put the access problem itself on the record. Scoring high on this domain means an entity sits at the point where the executive's information meets Congress's right to it: a committee chair, a cleared staff director, an IG, or a member who forced a vote.

entities.label: Records & Archives
entities.sub: Legal-procedural domain - the statutory fight over custody, transfer and destruction of the paper
entities.desc: Whoever controls the records controls the history, and this is the one front on which the disclosure movement has produced enacted law. Subtitle C of the FY2024 National Defense Authorization Act (P.L. 118-31) created, in Section 1841, an Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Collection at the National Archives; in Section 1842, an affirmative duty on every government office to review, identify and transmit UAP records to NARA; and in Section 1843, grounds for postponement - a framework in which withholding is temporary and must be justified rather than permanent and unexplained. The model is the President John F. Kennedy Assassination Records Collection Act of 1992, which is why the Senate's original UAP Disclosure Act of 2023 also proposed an independent Review Board with the power to order release over agency objection; that Review Board and the eminent-domain provision over recovered material were stripped before enactment. What survived is a records statute without an independent adjudicator, which places the postponement decision back inside the agencies that hold the records. The stakes are set by the documented history: GAO found in 1995 that Roswell Army Air Field's outgoing messages for 1946-1949 had been destroyed with no destruction certificate. Scoring high on this domain means an entity holds, transfers, withholds or destroys records - or wrote the law governing those acts.

entities.label: Freedom of Information Practice
entities.sub: Procedural domain - the request, the appeal, the Glomar, and what survives the exemptions
entities.desc: The Freedom of Information Act is the only routine instrument by which a private citizen can compel a federal agency to produce a record, and almost every primary document on this board arrived through it. Its limits are as instructive as its yield. Exemption 1 shields properly classified national defence information; Exemption 3 shields information withheld by other statute - including the National Security Agency Act, which NSA has successfully invoked to refuse even to describe its UFO-related holdings; and the Glomar response permits an agency to refuse to confirm or deny that responsive records exist at all. In Citizens Against UFO Secrecy v. NSA the courts sustained NSA's withholding of the overwhelming majority of its UFO-related documents on the strength of the Yeates affidavit, a filing whose own redacted form is a documented artifact of the concealment. The structural gap this board turns on is that FFRDC and prime-contractor records are contractor records, not agency records, and are outside FOIA entirely - so material that moves from a government shelf to a contractor shelf moves out of the statute's reach without ever being classified higher. Scoring high on this domain means an entity litigates, processes, or is the subject of these requests.

entities.label: Legal Doctrine & Liability
entities.sub: Legal domain - non-disclosure agreements, state secrets, amnesty, and the whistleblower's exposure
entities.desc: The law is the terrain on which a witness decides whether to speak, and the terrain is tilted. A person read into a special access programme signs a non-disclosure agreement with criminal exposure attached; the Intelligence Community Whistleblower Protection Act gives a lawful channel to the Inspector General but no protection at all for a disclosure made outside it; and the state secrets privilege can end a civil case before discovery without the court ever seeing the material. Against that stack, the disclosure movement's legislative answer has been amnesty and channel-building: the Senate's 2023 UAP Disclosure Act proposed immunity structures for contractors and personnel holding recovered material, and the UAP Whistleblower Protection Act - introduced as H.R. 10111 in the 118th Congress and reintroduced as H.R. 5060 on 29 August 2025 in the 119th - is an attempt to build a channel that does not run through the agencies being investigated. The documented cost of the current arrangement is visible in the DoD Inspector General's own product: DODIG-2023-109 exists because personnel used the IG channel, and its unclassified summary is nearly the whole of what the public received. Scoring high on this domain means an entity is a lawyer, litigant, adjudicator or drafter shaping what a witness may lawfully say.

entities.label: Litigation
entities.sub: Adversarial domain - the courtroom as a discovery instrument, and its documented ceiling
entities.desc: Litigation is the only mechanism on this board that can compel a sworn answer from an unwilling government witness, which is why so much effort has gone into it and why the results are so thin. The canonical run is Citizens Against UFO Secrecy v. NSA, in which a FOIA suit reached the D.C. Circuit and the Supreme Court denied certiorari in March 1982, leaving intact NSA's refusal to release the substance of its holdings on the strength of a classified affidavit the plaintiffs never saw. CAUS returned to court against the Department of Defense and reached the Ninth Circuit in 2001. The other documented route is the tort claim: Betty Cash, Vickie Landrum and Colby Landrum sued the United States in the Southern District of Texas over injuries they attributed to a December 1980 encounter, and the case was dismissed in August 1986 on the government's showing that no such craft was operated by any agency. Both patterns illustrate the ceiling - a court will not order the production of a thing the government swears does not exist, and the swearing is itself unreviewable in practice. Scoring high on this domain means an entity brought, defended or decided such a case.

entities.label: Legislative Process
entities.sub: Procedural domain - where UAP language is written, weakened and killed
entities.desc: Legislation is where the disclosure fight has produced its only binding outcomes and its most instructive defeats, and the mechanism of the defeats matters more than their fact. The UAP Disclosure Act of 2023, carried as Division I of the Senate-passed FY2024 NDAA with ten sections, would have created an independent Review Board with authority to compel release and an eminent domain provision over recovered technologies of unknown origin held by any person. What emerged from conference and became law in P.L. 118-31 was Subtitle C - a records collection at NARA, a duty to transmit, and postponement grounds - with the Review Board and eminent domain removed. The removal happened in conference, where authorship is diffuse and no recorded vote attaches, which is the characteristic signature of this domain: UAP provisions rarely lose on the floor, they lose in the seam between chambers. The fight continued through the FY2025 NDAA's Section 6802 sunset of the historical-record audit requirements and into the FY2026 and FY2027 cycles. Scoring high on this domain means an entity drafts, sponsors, amends or strips this language - and stripping counts as much as sponsoring.

entities.desc: This domain isolates what is enacted from what was merely proposed, because the difference is the whole of the disclosure movement's leverage. The binding corpus is small and can be listed: the FY2022 NDAA provision that stood up the Airborne Object Identification and Management Synchronization Group and its successor office; the FY2023 NDAA language establishing AARO's statutory mandate and a secure reporting mechanism with protection against reprisal for current and former personnel and contractors; and Subtitle C of the FY2024 NDAA (P.L. 118-31), Sections 1841 through 1843, creating the UAP Records Collection at NARA with an affirmative agency duty to transmit and defined grounds for postponement. Everything else - the Review Board, eminent domain over recovered material, contractor amnesty, standalone whistleblower protection - remains proposed. The practical consequence is that the executive branch currently owes Congress reports and owes NARA records, but owes no independent body an answer, and no statute yet compels the surrender of a physical object. entities.label: Materials Science & Analysis
entities.sub: Technical domain - metallurgy, microstructure and isotopics as the only falsifiable test available
entities.desc: Materials analysis is the single place where the central claim could be settled by measurement rather than by testimony, which is why both sides of the argument have converged on it. The falsifiable signature is isotopic: terrestrial elements occur in well-characterised isotope ratios set by solar system formation and by known industrial enrichment processes, so a sample whose ratios lie outside that envelope, and outside the known list of processes that can shift them, would be very difficult to explain conventionally. Garry Nolan, Jacques Vallée and colleagues published the methodology for exactly this test in Progress in Aerospace Sciences in 2022, setting out the instrumental techniques - including secondary ion mass spectrometry - applicable to characterising unusual materials for aerospace forensics. The results so far do not support the claim: AARO's January 2026 supplement reports Oak Ridge National Laboratory found a specimen from Ohio to be a conventional aluminium-silicon casting alloy with large grain sizes, interconnected porosity and needle-like silicon precipitates - defects, not exotica. The dual-use route matters here too, because the national laboratories that would perform such analysis are the same ones that perform nuclear forensics under Restricted Data controls. entities.label: Intelligence Tradecraft & Analysis
entities.sub: Methodological domain - collection management, source validation and the analytic habits this subject breaks
entities.desc: Intelligence analysis has a well-developed methodology for exactly this problem - a low-volume, high-consequence phenomenon with contaminated reporting - and applying it honestly is the discipline this board tries to import. The core tools are indications and warning analysis, source validation and the separation of collection gaps from analytic conclusions; the characteristic failure mode is treating an absence of collection as evidence of absence. ODNI's June 2021 preliminary assessment is an unusually candid document on precisely this point, stating that the limited and inconsistent quality of available reporting - not the phenomena themselves - was the principal obstacle to characterisation. The domain's most productive application in open literature is the indications analysis of UAP reporting against the United States atomic warfare complex published by Hancock, Porritt and Grosvenor, which uses a standard intelligence method on an unclassified corpus. The dual-use route is that the tradecraft used to validate a source is the same tradecraft used to discredit one, and a counterintelligence organisation possesses both. entities.label: Funding Channels
entities.sub: Financial domain - how money reaches an unacknowledged programme and why it cannot be traced
entities.desc: Money is the most auditable thing a concealed programme touches, and this is where the board's hardest evidence should eventually come from. The documented channels are all ordinary: classified programme elements carried in the defence budget as a single line with no descriptive text; general transfer authority, exercised annually under provisions such as Sections 8005 and 8006 of the Department of Defense Appropriations Acts, which lets the Department move substantial sums between accounts after enactment; Military Interdepartmental Purchase Requests, which move money between agencies without a new appropriation; contractor Independent Research and Development, which is company money reimbursed as an allowable overhead cost and is therefore government-funded work with no government line item; and the unvouchered expenditure authority of 50 U.S.C. 3510, under which the head of an agency may account for spending by certificate alone. The reason this is more than theory is that the Department of Defense has never passed a clean financial audit; the DoD Inspector General reported in 2016 that Army General Fund adjustments were not adequately documented or supported, and the audit findings have continued through the FY2025 cycle. Scoring high on this domain means an entity moves, certifies or conceals money.

entities.label: Black Budget & Unaccounted Funds
entities.sub: Financial domain - the audit failure as an enabling condition rather than a scandal
entities.desc: This domain narrows d-funding to a single question: how much money moves through the Department of Defense without a traceable link between appropriation and expenditure, and could a programme live inside that gap. The auditable facts are that the Department of Defense has never passed a full financial statement audit, that its own Inspector General has repeatedly documented unsupported journal voucher adjustments, and that the accounting standard for such adjustments is set out in the DoD Financial Management Regulation rather than in any statute Congress votes on annually. The academic work in this space is Mark Skidmore's, conducted at Michigan State University, which aggregated unsupported adjustments across multiple years of departmental financial reports and produced totals in the tens of trillions of dollars of gross adjustment volume - a figure that must be stated carefully, because gross adjustments are not missing money and conflating the two is the fastest way to lose an argument. The correct claim is narrower and stronger: the Department cannot demonstrate where its money went, and an entity that cannot demonstrate where its money went cannot demonstrate that none of it funded an unacknowledged programme. entities.label: International & Allied Programs
entities.sub: Comparative domain - what other states have admitted, and what their disclosures imply about ours
entities.desc: Other governments have made admissions the United States has not, and the comparison is one of the board's most useful instruments because it establishes what an official programme looks like when it is not concealed. France has run GEIPAN, a publicly funded investigative unit inside the national space agency CNES at Toulouse, since 1977 - with a published classification scheme, published statistics and a case archive open to the public, of which the category for cases that remain unexplained after full investigation is the operative one. Brazil transferred its military UFO files to the Arquivo Nacional, making them citizen-accessible, and its 1986 air force incident is documented in that archive. Chile's air force ran CEFAA under named officers who spoke on the record. The comparative point is decisive: none of these disclosures produced the harms the American concealment argument depends on, which shifts the burden onto the party claiming that only the United States cannot afford transparency. The allied-intelligence complication is real too - a programme shared under bilateral arrangements is protected by originator control, giving every partner a veto over release. timeline.label: Roswell announces, Fort Worth retracts
timeline.text: Roswell Army Air Field publicly announces that the 509th Bomb Group has come into possession of a flying disc. The material is flown to Eighth Air Force headquarters at Fort Worth, where it is presented to the press the same day as a weather balloon and radar target. Four official explanations for the event will follow over the next fifty years.

timeline.label: A foreign official records the American classification level
timeline.text: Wilbert B. Smith, a radio engineer in Canada's Department of Transport, writes an internal memorandum to the Controller of Telecommunications stating that the flying saucer subject is classified higher in the United States than the hydrogen bomb and that a small group is studying it. Its evidentiary value is its provenance: a foreign government official reporting internally, not a claimant addressing the public.

timeline.label: The Robertson Panel recommends a debunking programme
timeline.text: A CIA Office of Scientific Intelligence panel recommends that the national security agencies strip UFOs of their special status through a programme of mass-media 'training and debunking', and that civilian UFO groups be watched because of their potential influence on mass thinking. This is the documented origin point of the psychological-operations domain.

timeline.label: An agency whose existence is a secret
timeline.text: The National Reconnaissance Office is established with its very existence classified - a status maintained until September 1992. For thirty-one years the legally required answer to whether the organisation existed was no, which is the documented proof that a categorical official denial can be false and lawful at the same time.

timeline.label: The Condon Report closes the official file
timeline.text: The University of Colorado study directed by Edward Condon publishes 'Scientific Study of Unidentified Flying Objects', including Martin Altschuler's chapter on atmospheric electricity and plasma interpretations. Project Blue Book is terminated the following year, ending official American investigation for the next four decades.

timeline.label: Federal funding of anomalous cognition begins
timeline.text: Harold Puthoff and Russell Targ begin remote viewing work at Stanford Research Institute under federal sponsorship. The programme runs through Grill Flame, Center Lane, Sun Streak and Star Gate until 1995, establishing beyond argument that the US government funds research of this kind for decades at a time before terminating it and denying it produced anything.

timeline.label: The courts sustain the NSA wall
timeline.text: The D.C. Circuit upholds NSA's withholding of its UFO-related holdings in Citizens Against UFO Secrecy v. NSA, on the strength of a classified affidavit the plaintiffs never see; certiorari is denied in March 1982. This sets the practical ceiling on FOIA litigation in this field.

timeline.label: The Majestic-12 film arrives
timeline.text: Unsolicited film purporting to show an Eisenhower-era briefing document on recovered craft is delivered to Jaime Shandera. The FBI investigates and its file records an AFOSI assessment that the documents are bogus. Whatever their origin, their circulation imposes a permanent evidentiary tax on every genuine document in the field.

timeline.label: GAO finds the records destroyed
timeline.text: Responding to a request from Congressman Steven Schiff, GAO reports that Roswell Army Air Field outgoing messages for 1946-1949 were destroyed with no disposition authority and no destruction certificate on file. The destruction itself, documented by the government's own auditor, is the finding.

timeline.label: CIA concedes the false explanations
timeline.text: CIA historian Gerald K. Haines publishes 'CIA's Role in the Study of UFOs, 1947-90' in Studies in Intelligence, recording that U-2 and OXCART flights accounted for over half of late-1950s and 1960s reports and that Air Force investigators knowingly gave false explanations to the public. A documented admission of deliberate deception, from the deceiving agency.

timeline.label: DIA buys the physics
timeline.text: The Defense Intelligence Agency issues solicitation HHM402-08-R-0211 for the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program. The resulting contract produces thirty-eight Defense Intelligence Reference Documents on metric engineering, wormholes, antigravity and field effects on human tissue - the tier-1 evidence that a US agency paid to study the physics a recovered craft would require.

timeline.label: The conversion is considered
timeline.text: An Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence information memorandum records review of a special access programme request relating to AATIP. This is the documented moment at which a FOIA-visible programme was considered for conversion into an invisible one.

timeline.label: The Pentagon authenticates the imagery
timeline.text: The Department of Defense formally releases FLIR1, GIMBAL and GOFAST, confirming the videos are genuine while stating the phenomena in them remain unidentified. The government thereby authenticates the evidence and declines to explain it - the exact posture the disclosure movement has been arguing against ever since.

timeline.label: Three witnesses under oath
timeline.text: David Grusch, David Fravor and Ryan Graves testify under oath before the House Oversight Committee. Grusch describes a multi-decade retrieval and reverse-engineering programme reported to him by individuals he named to the Intelligence Community Inspector General; Fravor and Graves describe what they personally observed with sensor corroboration.

timeline.label: The Review Board is stripped in conference
timeline.text: P.L. 118-31 is enacted with Subtitle C - a UAP Records Collection at NARA, an agency duty to transmit, and grounds for postponement. The independent Review Board and the eminent domain provision over recovered technologies, both passed by the Senate as Division I of H.R. 2670, are removed in conference where no recorded vote attaches.

timeline.label: AARO answers on the record
timeline.text: AARO publishes Volume I of its historical record report, concluding it found no empirical evidence that the US government or private companies have reverse-engineered extraterrestrial technology. The report is catalogued here in full: its scope, its access and its methodology are the parts a hostile audit turns on.

timeline.label: The Inspector General reports, mostly classified
timeline.text: The DoD Inspector General releases an unclassified summary of DODIG-2023-109, its evaluation of the Department's actions regarding UAP. The evaluation was initiated on personnel complaints; the public receives the summary.

timeline.label: A signals technologist takes AARO
timeline.text: Jon Kosloski, a senior National Security Agency researcher, is named to lead AARO - placing the government's UAP analytic hub under someone whose professional formation is in the collection discipline that holds the most relevant withheld data.

timeline.label: Pre-Sputnik plates, nuclear correlation
timeline.text: Bruehl and Villarroel publish in Scientific Reports that transients in the Palomar Observatory Sky Survey may be associated with nuclear testing and with reports of unidentified anomalous phenomena. The data are photographic plates exposed between 1949 and 1957 and cannot have been contaminated by satellites.

timeline.label: Oversight returns to whistleblower protection
timeline.text: The House Oversight Committee holds 'Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection', following the reintroduction of the UAP Whistleblower Protection Act as H.R. 5060 on 29 August 2025. The 2025-2026 phase of the fight is procedural rather than revelatory.

timeline.label: Oak Ridge returns a conventional result
timeline.text: AARO publishes its Aluminum Materials Analysis Supplement, reporting that Oak Ridge National Laboratory found a specimen recovered near Flint Ridge, Ohio to match conventional aluminium-silicon casting alloys, with casting defects and no radioactive emissions. The materials domain's most recent test returned negative, and the board records that.

timeline.label: An artifact-search advocate inside the tent
timeline.text: Avi Loeb publishes his account of agreeing to lead a UAP Science Advisory Council for the US government, after the Disclosure Foundation announced on 14 June 2026 that he had been asked to assemble and chair a twelve-member multidisciplinary council. It is a directive-layer creation rather than a statutory one, and can be unmade the same way.

timeline.label: The House votes a records framework
timeline.text: The House approves an amendment offered by Rep. Eric Burlison creating a framework for UAP records disclosure - the records domain remaining the only front on which the disclosure movement reliably moves legislation.

Until people are scored on them they carry no graph weight, and a later pass should backfill domains[] on existing person records - the aviators dossier in particular should almost certainly carry d-signals, and the scientists dossier d-chem and d-astro.

THE C AXIS IS UNDER-EVIDENCED ON EXACTLY THE DOMAINS THAT MATTER MOST. d-legacy, d-recovery, d-reverse-engineering and d-bio are scored C3 on the strength of sworn testimony (tier 2) rather than primary documents (tier 1). That is honest grading, not a defect, but it means the board's central claim currently rests on one hearing. The research that would change this is contract and facility-clearance data, not more testimony.

NO PRIMARY DOCUMENT HAS BEEN LOCATED FOR THE FUNDING DOMAIN'S CENTRAL CLAIM. d-funding and d-money describe channels that demonstrably exist - transfer authority, MIPRs, IRAD, 50 U.S.C. 3510 unvouchered expenditure - and an audit failure that demonstrably exists. What is missing is any document connecting a specific dollar to a specific concealed activity. Until that exists the funding argument establishes possibility, not fact, and the dossiers say so.

SKIDMORE'S FIGURES ARE CITED AS GROSS ADJUSTMENTS, NOT MISSING MONEY, AND THE DISTINCTION IS LOAD-BEARING. The d-money dossier states this explicitly because conflating the two is the fastest way to lose the argument. A dedicated pass should locate Skidmore's published papers directly rather than relying on the DoD OIG findings that underpin them; no direct citation to his work was verified for this file.

TWO ROSWELL AIR FORCE REPORTS ARE CITED BY TITLE WITH DATING UNCERTAINTY. 'The Roswell Report: Fact vs. Fiction in the New Mexico Desert' is variously dated 1994 and 1995 across sources in the corpus; the DTIC copy cited here is dated 1995. 'The Roswell Report: Case Closed' is firmly 24 June 1997. A records pass should pin the first date to a publication record.

THE COMETA REPORT IS DESCRIBED IN THE l-paris AND l-france DOSSIERS WITHOUT A VERIFIED URL. The 1999 French report 'Les OVNI et la Defense' is real and well attested but no authoritative online copy was verified during this pass, so it appears in prose rather than in claims[] or sources[]. It should be sourced properly before any claim is built on it.

FIFTY-FOUR LOCATION IDS WERE DANGLING ACROSS THE CORPUS AND ARE NOW DEFINED, BUT TWENTY OF THEM ARE THIN BY DESIGN. The congressional home-district anchors (l-tompkinsville, l-glenbeulah, l-oro-valley and the rest) carry accurate but minimal dossiers deliberately: committee assignments and hearing roles belong on the person records in congress-house.json, and duplicating them here would create two places to get them wrong. Where a member's specific committee role could not be verified in this pass, the dossier says 'in the period covered by this board's congressional dossier' rather than asserting a role.

THREE LOCATION IDS ARE PURE ALIASES AND SHOULD BE COLLAPSED: l-washington-dc into l-dc (142 inbound references versus 2), l-lasvegas into l-las-vegas, and l-cambridge-ma into l-cambridge. They are defined here only so that no edge dangles before the merge pass runs.

THE d-consciousness DOSSIER IS THE BOARD'S WEAKEST AND IS TIERED C DELIBERATELY. Its only tier-1 content is that the government funded Star Gate for twenty-three years and commissioned Kit Green's DIRD on neurological field effects. The substantive claim - that observation is coupled to the phenomenon - has no primary support and is recorded as a tier-3 personnel-continuity inference. If the board wants to argue it, that argument has to be built from somewhere other than this file.

NO DOMAIN-LEVEL SCORING RUBRIC IS PUBLISHED. Each domain dossier explains what a high score means for that domain in prose, but there is no cross-domain calibration table, so a C3 on d-materials and a C3 on d-bio are not guaranteed to mean the same distance from custody. A calibration pass across all fifty domains would make the axis scores comparable; until then they are ordinal within a domain and only roughly comparable across domains.

AARO's VOLUME II HISTORICAL RECORD REPORT WAS NOT LOCATED IN THIS PASS. Volume I (February 2024) is cited throughout. NDAA FY2025 Section 6802 sunsets the audit requirements attached to the historical record report, which suggests the reporting obligation's status changed after 2024; the current state of Volume II and of the sunset's effect should be established directly from AARO and from P.L. 118-159's full text before any claim is made about it.
